title: Sunlit annotated reads — inference papers + conference scraps
content:
Quick TL;DR:
- Skimmed 4 papers + two conference talks. Common theme: getting long-context for production with small latency cost and predictable quality.
- Rough priorities: 1) lightweight prefix/KV compaction, 2) eviction-aware batching, 3) quantization stability checks on long-context copies.

Notes to self (informal):
- These are messy — mostly ideas + TODOs for small experiments I can run on a single 4-GPU Dedicated node.
- Keep focus on stuff that maps to Redwood runtime primitives: KV cache layout, shard placement, kernel selection. If it needs infra changes, flag early.

Papers / talks skimmed (one-liners + what I care about):
1) "Adaptive KV Compaction for Long-context Models" (arXiv, 2026) — link above.
   - Key idea: compress older KV entries with a cheap lossy transform (local PCA-like projection) and keep recent tokens full precision.
   - Pros: reduces memory footprint and cache-miss cost.
   - Cons: needs decode-time re-projection or accept small distro shift.
   - My notes: worth prototyping as an offline transform on saved caches first. Can we do compacted-KV fallback when memory pressure triggers? Map to Redwood Optimize suggestion: "cache-tiering".

2) "Eviction-aware batching" (NeurIPS talk notes)
   - Idea: batch formation should consider upcoming eviction cost (i.e., avoid creating huge batches that will cause KV reshuffle across shards).
   - Implementation trick: add a lightweight signal to request headers about "sticky" vs "ephemeral" contexts so scheduler can keep sticky ones on same worker.
   - My thought: tie this to per-customer route-policy in Console; experiment by adding a flag to synthetic load generator.

3) "Quantization regimes for stable long-context inference" (workshop paper)
   - Observed: int8/distillation quant has small immediate perplexity hit but larger degradation when retrieving long prefixes repeatedly.
   - Mitigation: keep attention/softmax layers at higher precision, quantize MLP only.
   - Actionable: add a small eval harness comparing 8-bit vs hybrid for our internal long-context prompt set (use evals from /evals/long-context-set).

4) "Mixture-of-Experts for KV sharding" (poster)
   - High-level: route different queries to specialized KV shards/experts to reduce cross-shard traffic.
   - Heuristic routing worked for thematic sessionization.
   - Concern: adds routing overhead and need for stateful sticky sessions.
   - Note: Could be a later-stage research spike; not necessary for immediate cost wins.

Conference takeaways (informal):
- Everyone is converging on multi-tier caches: small fast head + large slow store + policy to rehydrate. Think Redwood Dedicated burst capacity + prefix cache.
- There is appetite for offering "cache profiles" in product (e.g., aggressive-compact, default, quality-first). That matches Optimize feature ideas.

Actionable experiments (quick list):
- EXP-001: Offline compact-KV pipeline
  - Script: sample slowest 10% of KV entries from traces, run PCA compression, measure re-projection error on downstream logits.
  - Metrics: delta-perplexity, token latency for rehydration, memory saved.
  - Owner: me. Target: 1 week prototype.
  - Linked: GH PR above.

- EXP-002: Eviction-aware batch scheduler toy
  - Change: add "sticky" flag to synthetic requests; modify local scheduler to prefer co-locating sticky sessions.
  - Measure: cross-shard traffic metric, tail latency under mixed workload.
  - Owner: Leila.

- EXP-003: Quant-stability eval harness
  - Run: hybrid-quant vs full-fp16 on 200 long-context prompts (5000-10000 tokens).
  - Metric: perplexity drift over session length + hallucination score on RAG subset.
  - Owner: Mira.

Open questions / things to check quickly:
- How much real traffic has long-session reuse today? Need to ask infra: query usage retention window. TODO: ticket JIRA-OPS-1298 assigned to infra for real metrics.
- If we compact KV, what's the serialization compatibility story across model version rollouts? Need to check model format/version headers.
- Cost calculus: estimate cost-per-token saved vs engineering effort. Simple rule: if memory saving > 20% and perf hit < 1% perplexity for key evals, escalate.

Random scribbles / heuristics that felt right in talk:
- "Compaction happens on coldest layer first" — compress lower-value kv (farther in time) but only in MLP subspace.
- Consider a small "meta-key" per session that summarizes session semantics (topic embedding) to help routing without full KV transfer. Could be 32-d vector.

Links I want to keep handy:
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01234 (adaptive kv compaction)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/42 (prototype code)
- Slack thread (internal): slack://thread/CRY8u9f0 on "long-context-opportunities"

Next steps before Monday 2026-04-05 sync:
- Push EXP-001 prototype branch, add quick readme.
- Ask infra for long-session metric (JIRA-OPS-1298).
- Draft short one-pager for product: three cache profiles and suggested defaults.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short and rework into two deliverables: 1) quickplay experiment runbook, 2) product one-pager.

End of messy notes. Probably missing citations and many half-baked heuristics. Will iterate after experiments.
